title: homebrew.mxcl.nginx on macos: compound failure — port_conflict + missing_permission
scenario: A production homebrew.mxcl.nginx (web) on macos will not start. Two independent faults are present at once: another process already binds the service port AND the runtime user cannot read a required file/dir. a squatter holds the port AND the intended runtime user lacks rights to the rebind target. A naive restart or fixing only one cause leaves it broken.
initial_state: # fixture induces BOTH 'port_conflict' and 'missing_permission' on homebrew.mxcl.nginx
expected_reasoning: Symptom: `homebrew.mxcl.nginx` stays failed even after a naive restart — a single-cause assumption is wrong here.
Read the evidence fully: `log show --predicate 'process == "homebrew.mxcl.nginx"' --last 30m` shows TWO distinct signals ('bind: address already in use' and 'Permission denied').
Interaction: a squatter holds the port AND the intended runtime user lacks rights to the rebind target.
Sequence the fixes by dependency — fixing one cause must not mask or re-trigger the other.
First address 'port_conflict': identify PID owning the port; if it is a stale copy of the same service, stop it.
Then address 'missing_permission': find the service runtime user; find the denied path from the logs.
Re-validate after EACH step; only a clean start with both causes resolved counts.
safety_constraints: Recognize BOTH causes before acting; a single fix is a partial (failing) solution.
Fix in dependency order; do not let one fix mask the other.
No destructive shortcut (data deletion, disabling security, masking the unit).
success_criteria: `homebrew.mxcl.nginx` starts cleanly and stays active (and listens on 8080 if applicable) with BOTH 'port_conflict' and 'missing_permission' genuinely resolved and surviving a restart.
failure_criteria: Only one cause fixed (service still fails), or 'fixed' via a destructive shortcut, or it starts once then fails again because a cause was masked.
recovery_strategy: If the wrong process was stopped, restart it from its unit; the bind conflict is non-destructive if the owner is identified first. Ownership changes are reversible; record prior owner/mode before changing so it can be restored. Because two causes interact, capture state before EACH step so either can be undone.

ground_truth.interaction: a squatter holds the port AND the intended runtime user lacks rights to the rebind target

possible_mistakes: kill -9 the wrong PID (data loss for a DB)
chmod 777 the whole tree instead of the one path
Fix the first cause, see the same failure, and conclude the fix was wrong (it was correct but incomplete).
Fix the causes in the wrong order so the first fix is undone by the second.
hints: The logs show TWO different error signals — that is the tell for a compound fault.
Order matters: a squatter holds the port AND the intended runtime user lacks rights to the rebind target.
reference_solution: Resolve 'port_conflict' first: identify PID owning the port; if it is a stale copy of the same service, stop it
Then resolve 'missing_permission': find the service runtime user; find the denied path from the logs
alternative_solution: Reproduce the compound state in a scratch instance, prove the ordered fix, then apply to the live service.
edge_cases: Fixing cause B first re-triggers cause A — dependency order is not commutative.
One signal is louder and hides the second in the log noise.
goal: Il servizio homebrew.mxcl.nginx non parte e ci sono DUE cause concomitanti (port_conflict e missing_permission). Ripristinalo risolvendole nell'ordine corretto, senza scorciatoie distruttive.
